title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 49 (Calls on Shares of Same Class to Be Made on Uniform Basis)

content.overview: Section 49 requires that where any calls for further share capital are made on shares of a class, such calls shall be made on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class.
content.glance: Calls for further capital on a class of shares must be made uniformly on all shares of that class.
content.study: Where any calls for further share capital are made on the shares of a class, such calls shall be made on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class. The rule prevents discriminatory calls within the same class. Current-law framing: identify the class and the call; test uniformity across all shares of that class.

sections.heading: Uniform Calls
sections.body: Calls for further share capital on shares of a class must be made on a uniform basis on all shares of that class.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: The rule protects equality of treatment among holders of the same class when further capital is called.

provisions.title: Calls on shares of same class to be made on uniform basis

examples.title: Uniform call
examples.body: The company calls ₹10 per share on all partly paid equity shares of the same class. Section 49 is complied with.

examples.title: Discriminatory call
examples.body: The board calls further capital only on some shareholders within the same class. Section 49 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company call different amounts on different shares of the same class?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 49 requires calls on a uniform basis on all shares falling under that class.

distinctions.title: Uniform calls (s. 49) vs acceptance of unpaid share capital (s. 50)
distinctions.left: How calls must be structured within a class
distinctions.right: Company’s power to accept unpaid capital not yet called

rows.right: Voluntary payment in advance of calls

misconceptions.trap: The company may call only selected holders within a class for convenience.
misconceptions.correction: Section 49 mandates uniform calls on all shares of that class.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 49 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the class. II. Identify the call. III. Test uniformity across the class. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class; call terms; uniformity or discrimination; precise relief.
